result.final_text:
## What this letter says
Your son is 14 months old. He was in hospital for Kawasaki disease. The letter says it is getting better (resolving).
His fever and rash have completely gone. He has no red eyes (conjunctivitis). He has no redness of the mouth lining (mucous membranes).
He had IVIG two times. His fever came back within 12 hours of the first dose. It did not come back after the second dose.
His heart scan (echocardiogram) was negative.
He is calmer. He is eating and drinking well by mouth.

## What you need to do
1. See your primary doctor in 2 to 3 days.
2. Go to the cardiology visit for a repeat heart scan (echo) in 4 to 6 weeks.
3. Give the medicines as listed below.
4. His activities and food and drink by mouth are "ad-lib" (as he wants).
5. Do not give him any vaccine for less than 11 months because of the IVIG. This includes all live virus vaccines.
6. The letter does not say if the 11 months starts now or from the IVIG. Please ask your doctor.

## Dates and medicines
**Dates**
- In 2 to 3 days: follow-up with your primary doctor.
- In 4 to 6 weeks: cardiology follow-up with an echo.

**Medicines (all new)**
- Aspirin, high dose: 340 milligrams, every 6 hours, for 1 day. Then switch to low dose aspirin.
- Aspirin, low dose: 40 milligrams, once a day, for 14 days. Start it after the 1 day of high dose.
- Prevacid: 15 milligrams, by mouth, once a day. It protects his stomach and bowel (GI) from the aspirin.

## Questions to ask your doctor
- What is IVIG, and why does it stop vaccines for 11 months?
- Does the 11 months start now or from the IVIG?
- What does the heart scan (echocardiogram) show, and what will the next one check?
- Which day do I switch from high dose to low dose aspirin?

## When to get urgent help
- If he gets any rashes or any fevers, go to your primary care doctor as soon as possible.

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
